title: Functions & domains
description: Connect function notation to inputs, outputs, and graphs. Explore intercepts, domain and range, then practice domain restrictions with individual checks.

sections.title: Interpret function notation
sections.text: Use the box model to name outputs, solve for inputs, and distinguish a function value from a change in values.

sections.title: Read relationships and graphs
sections.text: Connect a square’s side and perimeter, interpret the tortoise’s lead and intercepts, and test whether a relation is a function in each direction.

sections.title: Find domain and range
sections.text: Explore the original algebraic examples and read a graph with explicit open or closed endpoints.

sections.title: Practice domain restrictions
sections.text: Ten individually checked problems cover polynomials, rational expressions, square roots, combined restrictions, cancellation, physical limits, and discrete inputs.

sourceNote: Based on M3I2: Function Relations and Domain of Functions, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. Source scenarios and examples are adapted into interactive tools. The range of 1/(x² − 9) is corrected, and limiting cases and endpoint inclusion are explicit. The final domain practice set is original.

title: The box problem
description: Cut and fold one adjustable paper box. Link its dimensions, table, and graphs to volume, changes, target values, maximum volume, and exterior surface area.

sections.title: Cut, fold, and measure
sections.text: Control the cutout and fold angle, connect the paper net with a three-dimensional box, and distinguish physical boxes from limiting configurations.

sections.title: Build the model
sections.text: Derive base dimensions and volume, complete the original table, and connect graph points with measurements.

sections.title: Compare and solve
sections.text: Compare changes over intervals, find two cutouts for the same volume, and refine an estimate of maximum volume.

sections.title: Model surface area
sections.text: Count the five faces or subtract the four cutouts, then solve the final area-to-volume problem with adequate precision.

sourceNote: Based on M3I1: The Box Problem and Modeling Relationships, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC, with a link to the supplied GeoGebra Box Folding 3D activity. The folding toolbox and guided checks are original teaching adaptations. The final worked example’s premature rounding is corrected.

title: Absolute value & tolerance
description: Explore absolute value as distance through carpenter and model-airplane tolerances, interactive number lines, signed changes, and individual checks.

sections.title: From error to distance
sections.text: Compare a board’s actual length, signed error, and error magnitude. Translate its tolerance into an inclusive interval.

sections.title: Direction and endpoints
sections.text: Distinguish a positive change from an unsigned distance, and compare between-values conditions with two outward rays.

sections.title: Apply and translate
sections.text: Work through the model-airplane scenario and connect the original word conditions to inequalities and interval notation.

sections.title: Practice all representations
sections.text: Read four absolute value inequalities, identify boundaries, choose endpoint inclusion, and explore each solution set.

sections.title: Connect with the course assessment
sections.text: Compare exact-distance equations with inequalities, practice a second board-cutting scenario, and explain why a negative distance gives no real solutions.

sourceNote: Based on M2I7: Absolute Value and the linked Absolute Value course assessment, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. All ten PDF exercises are represented with adapted checks and interactive number lines, alongside selected assessment examples on exact distance and equations.

title: Distance & circles
description: Use one connected graph to build the distance formula from a right triangle, then trace points at a fixed distance to derive the circle equation. Explore the cell-tower scenarios with guided checks.

sections.title: Build a right triangle
sections.text: Locate the house and cell tower, identify horizontal and vertical separations, and distinguish signed coordinate changes from leg lengths.

sections.title: Derive and generalize the distance formula
sections.text: Apply the Pythagorean theorem, take the nonnegative square root, and compare the original and second towers.

sections.title: Trace and describe a circle
sections.text: Keep the tower fixed and the distance constant. Trace the boundary, then connect the geometry to the equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².

sections.title: Choose the right boundary point
sections.text: Solve for the point southeast of the tower, compare the two intersections, and distinguish a circle boundary from the coverage disk.

sourceNote: Based on M2I6: The Distance Formula and the Equation of a Circle, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. Original scenarios are included; the interactive graph and checks are teaching adaptations. The missing square root in the first displayed equality of Exercise 2(a) is corrected.

title: Exploring Average Speed
description: Explore average speed through six scenarios, adjustable graphs, individual answer checks, and mathematical explanations. This lesson saves responses in your browser.

sections.title: Concert and wedding trips
sections.text: Interpret average speed and use it to make predictions about distance and travel time.

sections.title: Average speed versus constant rate
sections.text: Measure distance and time, then compare two carts with the same whole-trip average and different motion. Select shorter intervals and check what the quotient does and does not tell you.

sections.title: Crosswalk
sections.text: Compare a curved distance graph with a constant-rate model using an adjustable secant line.

sections.title: Intersection
sections.text: Track starting position, direction changes, and the selected time interval.

sections.title: Practice
sections.text: Compare average speeds over successive intervals and check your reasoning.

sourceNote: Adapted from M2I5.pdf, Exploring Average Speed, Module 2: Investigation 5 Instructor Notes, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. Interactive graphs and the measurement exploration are adaptations.

title: Constant rates & proportionality
description: An interactive lesson on constant rates of change, linear functions, and proportional relationships. Explore the bike ride, pool, remote-control car, mixtures, cylinders, and candles.

sections.title: Identify quantities
sections.text: Classify quantities in the bike ride and decide which are fixed or varying.

sections.title: Build the constant-rate formula step by step
sections.text: Follow a six-step pool guide from paired measurements to corresponding changes, a rate per input unit, and a formula from a known point. Use individual checks, an adjustable graph, and a staged derivation.

sections.title: Connect changes, rates, and initial values
sections.text: Explore reciprocal rates and use Δy = mΔx to distinguish a change from a final value. Work through the pool observations and randomized self-checks.

sections.title: Explore constant rates on graphs
sections.text: Move initial and final points on five linear models, reverse intervals, and examine why a zero-length interval gives an undefined ratio.

sections.title: Distinguish proportional changes from proportional values
sections.text: Begin with an essential select-all checkpoint: which equations does a constant rate guarantee? Compare values with changes using explanations and a counterexample. Then resize a picture or square, compare pool depths, scale a mixture, and explore cylinders and candles.

sourceNote: Based on M2I3: Constant Rate of Change and Linear Functions and M2I4: Constant Rate of Change & Proportionality, Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. Scenario sources and adaptations are identified in the lesson. The Bob graph follows its labeled coordinates because the printed point placement is inconsistent.

title: Quantities & change
description: Identify measurable quantities, define variables, and connect a quantity’s value to its signed change. Explore graphs and reason through the tortoise-and-hare race and a walk to the car.

sections.title: Identify and define
sections.text: Classify ten candidates, explain which criteria fail, and write variable definitions for a marathon and a ball above a rooftop.

sections.title: Separate a value from its change
sections.text: Explore temperature readings, use ΔT = T_{final} − T_{initial}, and check your understanding with new practice values.

sections.title: Read change on a graph
sections.text: Move two points on walking, square-area, and reservoir graphs. Compare initial values, final values, and signed changes.

sections.title: Use the quantities in a story
sections.text: Work through the race and the walk to the car. Distinguish position, distance traveled, distance remaining, and signed lead.

sourceNote: Based on Module 2 Investigations 1 and 2 from Pathways Precalculus, ©2026 Rational Reasoning LLC. The lesson identifies original scenario text and adaptations. The walk-to-the-car activity is an added extension.
